title: Help for Employers, Employees and Those Looking for Jobs during COVID-19 Crisis
what_it_is: Help for Employers, Employees and Those Looking for Jobs during COVID-19 Crisis

sections.label: Work permit holder protections
sections.summary: Questions ask the Minister for Manpower about fair dismissal, unpaid salaries, return to home countries, communication of measures, and an advisory for work permit holders and employers, and about protecting workers facing contract termination and retrenchment.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) what measures are undertaken to ensure fair dismissal practices by employers of work permit holders who have been tested positive for COVID-19 and after the circuit breaker period; (b) what is the course of action for work permit holders who (i) have lost their jobs (ii) have salaries unpaid or (iii) wish to return to their countries of origin; (c) how have measures to safeguard employment and payment of salaries been communicated to (i) work permit holders and (ii) their employers; and (d) whether the Ministry will issue an advisory on (i) employment (ii) salaries (iii) fair dismissal practices and (iv) contract termination for all work permit holders and their employers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Manpower what is being done to better protect, assist and support workers, especially professionals, managers and executives, who face contract termination, disguised retrenchments and other job severance and managing excess manpower arrangements which affect their livelihood during this COVID-19 period.

sections.label: Labour market and job losses
sections.summary: Questions ask about the labour market situation, employment contraction, expected job losses when the Jobs Support Scheme expires, job creation initiatives, and support for employees terminated without retrenchment benefits; first quarter 2020 estimates showed a slight uptick in unemployment and retrenchments.

sentences.speaker: Mr Liang Eng Hwa
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) what is the latest labour market situation and the extent of contraction in local and foreign employment in the last three months; (b) what is the number of job losses expected in the next one year when the Jobs Support Scheme expires; and (c) what are the initiatives to support new job creations.

sentences.speaker: Ms Joan Pereira
sentences.text: asked the Minister for Manpower whether there are any plans to support employees who have been given notice by their employers to terminate their contracts but who have not received retrenchment benefits for terminations due to redundancies rather than poor performance.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: For the first quarter of 2020, preliminary estimates showed a slight uptick of our unemployment rate and retrenchments compared to the previous quarter, even though they remained lower than peaks experienced during the SARS outbreak and Global Financial Crisis.

sections.label: GDP contraction and job displacements
sections.summary: With Singapore's GDP expected to contract by between 4% and 7%, further job displacements should be expected.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: As Singapore's GDP is expected to contract by between 4% and 7%, we should be prepared for further job displacements.

sections.label: Penalties for disguised retrenchment
sections.summary: MOM can consider withdrawing Government support like JSS and suspending work pass privileges for companies found to have disguised retrenchments, and tripartite partners agreed retrenchment benefit may be re-negotiated or moderated in genuine financial difficulty.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: If a company is found to have disguised their retrenchments, MOM can and will consider withdrawing Government support like JSS and suspending their work pass privileges.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: The tripartite partners have therefore agreed that in instances of genuine financial difficulty for the employer, retrenchment benefit may be re-negotiated or moderated.

sections.label: Employer notification of cost-saving measures
sections.summary: MOM has required employers to submit notifications of cost-saving measures they intend to undertake to ensure fair and responsible implementation of tripartite advisories.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: To ensure fair and responsible implementation of tripartite advisories, MOM has required employers to submit notifications of cost-saving measures they intend to undertake.

sections.label: Salary support for migrant workers
sections.summary: Employers should not dismiss people for COVID-19, and must use Government levy rebates to give salary support to their migrant workers even if business is disrupted.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Employers do not dismiss people because they got the flu or dengue, and they should not do so with COVID-19 either.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: We have made clear to employers that even if business is disrupted, they must use the levy rebates that the Government has provided to give salary support to their migrant workers.

sections.label: Fair Consideration Framework strengthened
sections.summary: MOM made Fairness at Work its priority, strengthening the Fair Consideration Framework and stiffening penalties for discriminatory employers.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: At the start of the year, MOM had identified Fairness at Work as our priority.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: We strengthened the Fair Consideration Framework (FCF) and stiffened penalties for employers with discriminatory practices, whether for age or gender bias or for not giving qualified Singaporeans serious consideration for jobs.

sections.label: Upholding Fair Consideration Framework
sections.summary: The Fair Consideration Framework will continue to be upheld as a commitment to the people while more job pathways open.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Even as we work on opening up more pathways to jobs, we will continue to uphold the Fair Consideration Framework as a commitment to our people.

sections.label: Possible CPF contribution rate cuts
sections.summary: Further moves including possible CPF contribution rate cuts cannot be precluded, though cuts permanently reduce a person's retirement savings.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: I appreciate also the fact that he himself, in his capacity as a CEO, is responsible for many employees and he would naturally also want to see if there are ways that he can enable them to continue in employment.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: So, we are very mindful and at this juncture, we cannot preclude any further moves including the possibility of CPF contribution rate cuts in the future.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: But I would say also that for CPF rate cuts, while the intention may be temporary in nature, the loss to a person's ability to accumulate savings for retirement is permanent.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Once that savings opportunity is foregone, it cannot easily be reclaimed, and it usually takes a very long time to eventually restore whatever rates that have been cut.

sections.label: Handling disguised retrenchments
sections.summary: The speaker is heartened by answers on handling disguised retrenchments and MOM measures including withholding JSS against errant employers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: I am particularly heartened that she has answered my question on how we are going to better handle disguised retrenchments including situations where companies who are able to pay retrenchment benefits and execute disguised retrenchments will be taken to task if they do not do so.

sentences.speaker: Mr Patrick Tay Teck Guan (West Coast)
sentences.text: So, I am glad to hear the various executive measures by MOM as well as even withholding JSS will be enforced where needed against errant employers.

sections.label: Action against breaching employers
sections.summary: Where there is clear evidence of breach of guidelines or laws by an employer, action will be taken.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Where there is clear evidence of breach of guidelines or laws on the part of the employer, please be assured that we will take action.

sections.label: Work permit holder claims and support
sections.summary: The speaker asks how online salary and wrongful dismissal claim filing was communicated to work permit holders and whether employers must keep paying salaries and expenses.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I have two supplementary questions for the Minister.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: She mentioned TADM and we are aware of it; and given that in-person services for TADM and also that the Employment Claims Tribunal are currently suspended due to safe distancing measures, could I ask the Minister how has the Ministry communicated the online process of filing salary and wrongful dismissal claims to work permit holders.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: The second question is, there was a advisory dated 25 April 2020 regarding salary and leave arrangements during circuit breaker, where employers of work permit holders are responsible for their maintenance and upkeep.

sentences.speaker: Ms Anthea Ong (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As we exit the circuit breaker, for work permit holders who cannot work due to COVID-19 or the fact that their dormitories are being gazetted as isolation areas, could the Minister please clarify if employers of work permit holders must continue to pay for: one, their salaries; two, their living arrangements; three, their food expenses and also last but not least, miscellaneous expenses.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Wherever it is that the workers are living and including in the dormitories, the employers have primary responsibility.

sections.label: Employer salary and upkeep responsibility
sections.summary: Employers are responsible for salary and upkeep during the circuit breaker, but no blanket rule requires covering all workers' costs.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Even during this period of the circuit breaker, the employers have responsibility for salary and for upkeep.

sentences.speaker: Mrs Josephine Teo
sentences.text: Outside of that, there is no blanket to say that the employers must cover all of the workers' cost.

sections.label: Study on gender wage gap
sections.summary: An April 2020 study showed a ban reduced the gender wage gap in that state, prompting a question on MOM's study.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: In a study that was published in April 2020, it showed that this ban led to a reduction in the gender wage gap in in that state.

sentences.speaker: Mr Louis Ng Kok Kwang (Nee Soon)
sentences.text: So, could I ask whether MOM has studied the extent to which this declaration of last drawn salary contributes to the gender wage gap here in Singapore?
